Round 2 · Implementation · Medium

Ticket #01 — Event Registration

Difficulty: Medium

Context

You maintain registration for a campus career night. An event has a fixed number of places. A registration links one student to one event; active registrations use places, while cancelled records remain as history.

Practice report

Create career-night with capacity 1. Through post_registration, register student s1 as r1, cancel r1 through delete_registration, then submit student s2 as r2 for the same event.

Observation Current starter Expected
Result of the final registration request Status 409 Status 201
Who occupies the single place afterward Nobody; r1 is cancelled s2; r1 stays cancelled

These status values come from the supplied route adapter; no web server is needed to reproduce the report.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Active registrations alone consume capacity, and their count never exceeds the event's capacity. Cancelling one active registration frees one place.
  • A student cannot have two active registrations for the same event. A student whose earlier registration was cancelled can register again with a new ID.
  • A registration ID cannot replace an existing record. Missing required request fields or an unknown event are rejected without creating a registration.
  • Cancellation succeeds only for an existing active registration. An unknown or repeated cancellation leaves every stored registration unchanged.
  • Every rejected registration leaves the stored registrations unchanged.

Out of Scope

Keep the in-memory repository and route response shape. Event scheduling, payments, waitlists, and concurrent database transactions are outside this ticket.

Investigation

Reproduce the cancellation sequence through the route adapter and follow the request through service, repository, and model code. Add focused regression assertions for returned statuses and stored registration state; explain how they prove that one place is released and cannot be occupied twice.
